title: Two types of bodies in one background: equal fall and equal clock response

key_results.statement: Class: bodies of the class C with linear profiles, limiting coefficients of (8.26). Response per label $\varrho_i=g_{\eta,i}$ and $A^{(i)}_{k,\sigma}=\frac{d_{0,i}\tau_i^2}{M^{(i)}_k}(\sigma\mathcal F_i-m_ig_{m,i}-d^{(i)}_kg_{\eta,i})$.
Same class. $A^{(i)}_{k,+}$ is the same for all levels iff $(\mathrm L_i)$: $\mathcal F_i=m_i(g_{m,i}-g_{\eta,i})$; the value is $A^{(i)}=-v_i^2\varrho_i/d_{0,i}$.

Under $\lambda\to s\lambda$ and $X\to tX$ the quantities $\tau_i,\kappa_i,d_{0,i},v_i,\varrho_i,\varrho_i/d_{0,i},A^{(i)}_{k,+},A^{(i)}_{k,+}/v_i^2$ get the factors $1/s,1/(st),1/s,1/s^2,1,s,1/s^3,s$: only $\varrho_i$ is well defined; every ratio between the two types that exists is well defined, and for quantities that can vanish the pair $(q_1,q_2)$ up to a common positive factor is.

Same class. The two types fall alike from rest (FA) iff $(\mathrm L_1)$, $(\mathrm L_2)$ and $v_1^2\varrho_1/d_{0,1}=v_2^2\varrho_2/d_{0,2}\neq0$, that is $\kappa_1\tau_1^2g_{\eta,1}=\kappa_2\tau_2^2g_{\eta,2}\neq0$.

Same class. One non-zero value of $A^{(i)}_{k,\sigma}$ for all levels, both branches and both types iff $\mathcal F_i=0$, $g_{m,i}=g_{\eta,i}$ for $i=1,2$ and $v_1^2\varrho_1/d_{0,1}=v_2^2\varrho_2/d_{0,2}\neq0$.

Same class. The accelerations in position labels are equal for the two types and all levels iff $(\mathrm L_1)$, $(\mathrm L_2)$ and $\tau_1^2g_{\eta,1}=\tau_2^2g_{\eta,2}$; the statement is well defined but is not a statement about distances, and given FA it holds iff $\kappa_1=\kappa_2$.
Same class, ideal (wide-start) responses. RL: $\varrho_1=\varrho_2$ iff $g_{\eta,1}=g_{\eta,2}$; RD: $\varrho_1/d_{0,1}=\varrho_2/d_{0,2}$ iff $g_{\eta,1}/\kappa_1=g_{\eta,2}/\kappa_2$.
Same class. FA implies (RD iff $v_1=v_2$); RD implies (FA iff $(\mathrm L_1)$, $(\mathrm L_2)$, $\varrho_1\neq0$, $v_1=v_2$); neither of FA, RD implies the other.

Controls with $\kappa_1=\kappa_2$, $\tau_2=2\tau_1$, variant (a): K1 with $g_1=4g_2\neq0$ falls alike while $\varrho_1/d_{0,1}=4\varrho_2/d_{0,2}$; K2 with $g_1=g_2\neq0$ has equal responses while $A^{(2)}=4A^{(1)}$.

Class: two Model D bodies coupled to one sharp stationary field with $\Phi\varphi=\gamma\varphi$. The bodies and the medium evolve by $C_{\rm red}$, in which the rest and clock term of the type $i$ carries the factor $1+\gamma\theta_ix$.

Same class. Effective gradients $g_{m,i}=g_{\eta,i}=\gamma\theta_i$, $g_{\zeta,i}=0$, $\mathcal F_i=-\kappa_i\langle X\rangle$; the effective contracts are of the class C iff $|\gamma|L\max(|\theta_1|,|\theta_2|)<1$.

For fields with (N): common coupling for the fall is $\Theta_1=\Theta_2$ with $\Theta_i=v_i^2\theta_i/d_{0,i}$; then $A^{(i)}_{k,+}(\gamma)-A^{(i)}_{k,+}(\gamma')=-\Theta(\gamma-\gamma')$ for all levels and both types for every $\langle X\rangle$, and FA holds for $\langle X\rangle=0$, $\Theta\gamma\neq0$. Common coupling for the clocks is $\theta_1/d_{0,1}=\theta_2/d_{0,2}$. If (N) fails, neither is defined.
Class: bodies of the class C with $\tau_i>0$. The relative factor of the two bodies is detectable iff the medium is read and $X$ is not diagonal in the places of the medium.

Under the equivalence (5.20): $\tau_i,m_i,d^{(i)}_k,\mathcal F_i,\kappa_i,d_{0,i}$ are divided by $a_i$, $\lambda_{0,i}$ is multiplied by $a_i$, the gradients and $\varrho_i$ are unchanged, $v_i\to v_i/a_i^2$, $\varrho_i/d_{0,i}\to a_i\varrho_i/d_{0,i}$, $A^{(i)}_{k,\sigma}\to A^{(i)}_{k,\sigma}/a_i^3$.

Set $\mathfrak E_0$: an equivalent description that is again of the form of the setting (class C, linear profiles, one record operator) has $F'_i=F_i/a_i+c_i\mathbb 1$, hence $C'^{\rm eff}_i=C^{\rm eff}_i/a_i+c_i\mathbb 1$, and obeys (8.16).

Proven in the own-data form for all $C'\in\mathfrak E_1$ and in the transported form (starts of $C$; record vectors, hop distance, bound, mean position and rates of $C'$) for all $C'\in\mathfrak E_2$: with the medium read and $X$ not diagonal, FA, $v_1=v_2$, RL, RD and (4.24) have, for every contract of the class, the same truth value in $C$ and in $C'$; with $X$ diagonal or the medium not read, RL and (4.24) of each type have this for every contract, while FA, $v_1=v_2$ and RD do not have it for every contract (the contracts for which their truth value can be changed are given in (8.29)). For $C'\in\mathfrak E\setminus\mathfrak E_2$ FA, $v_1=v_2$ and RD are not defined, and only the label form (8.28) of RL and (4.24) is proven.

Medium not read, $C'\in\mathfrak E_2$ with $a_1=a_2\sqrt{v_1/v_2}$ (transported form; own-data form for $C'\in\mathfrak E_1$): $v'_1=v'_2$ for every pair, and then $A'^{(1)}_{k,+}=(v_2/v_1)^{3/2}A^{(1)}_{k,+}/a_2^3$, $A'^{(2)}_{k,+}=A^{(2)}_{k,+}/a_2^3$, $\varrho'_i=\varrho_i$, $\varrho'_1/d'_{0,1}=a_2\sqrt{v_1/v_2}\,\varrho_1/d_{0,1}$, $\varrho'_2/d'_{0,2}=a_2\varrho_2/d_{0,2}$; for $C'\in\mathfrak E\setminus\mathfrak E_2$ the bound $v'_i$ is not defined.

Medium not read. A description $C'\in\mathfrak E_2$ with FA in the transported form exists iff $(\mathrm L_1)$, $(\mathrm L_2)$ and $g_{\eta,1}g_{\eta,2}>0$; the condition is the same for $\mathfrak E_1$ with FA in the own-data form and for $\mathfrak E_0$; for $C'\in\mathfrak E\setminus\mathfrak E_2$ FA is not defined.

Relative factor not detectable, convention $v'_1=v'_2$ (defined on $\mathfrak E_2$): FA and RD become the one statement $(\mathrm L_1)$, $(\mathrm L_2)$ and $A^{(1)}/v_1^{3/2}=A^{(2)}/v_2^{3/2}\neq0$, which has the same truth value in $C$ and in every $C'\in\mathfrak E_2$ (transported form; own-data form for $C'\in\mathfrak E_1$).

Descriptions with body contracts $C^{\rm D}_i+\beta_ib_i$, a constant $\beta_0\mathbb 1$ on the bodies and the medium, and coupling $\theta_ib_i\otimes\Phi$ have the same $C$ iff $\theta'_i\Phi'^\circ=\theta_i\Phi^\circ$, $\beta'_i+\theta'_i\bar\varphi'=\beta_i+\theta_i\bar\varphi$, $C'_f=C_f+c\,\mathbb 1_f$ and $\beta'_0=\beta_0-c$ with a real $c$; condition (N): the interaction part $I=\sum_i\theta_ib_i\otimes\Phi^\circ$ is non-zero, that is $\Phi\notin\mathbb R\mathbb 1_f$ and $(\theta_1,\theta_2)\neq(0,0)$.

RD holds iff $n_2d_{0,2}\,n_1\varrho_1=n_1d_{0,1}\,n_2\varrho_2$ for all interval sizes $1\le n_1,n_2\le2L$; realizable intervals of equal length exist iff $n_1\kappa_1=n_2\kappa_2$ for some such integers, otherwise RD compares the slopes only.

Class: the contract of the setting, bodies of the class C, $\tau_i>0$. With the medium not read, $(a_1,a_2;C')$ is an equivalence iff $C'=F_1/a_1+F_2/a_2+\Delta$ with $\Delta=\delta_0+Q_1\delta_1+Q_2\delta_2+\varepsilon_{12}Q_1Q_2$, $[\delta_j,X]=0$, all $a_1,a_2>0$; with the medium read, the equivalences are those of (5.19) with these $\Delta$ and diagonal $\delta_j$.

For every $C'\in\mathfrak E_2$ (the equivalent descriptions without a term between the two bodies, in which the record vectors in the medium are defined) and every start: hop distance $d_{0,i}/a_i$, bound $v_i/a_i^2$, rates $r_i/a_i$, $\varrho'_i=\varrho_i$, and the acceleration of the mean position is divided by $a_i^3$ at $\lambda'/a_i$. On $\mathfrak E_1$ ($\varepsilon_{12}=0$, $\langle\chi|\delta_i|\chi\rangle=0$) the effective body contracts are $C^{\rm eff}_i/a_i+c_i\mathbb 1$; $\mathfrak E_0\subset\mathfrak E_1\subset\mathfrak E_2\subset\mathfrak E$.

Asymptotic family of all results: $L\max(|g_{m,i}|,|g_{\eta,i}|,|g_{\zeta,i}|,|\mathcal F_i|/m_i)\ll1$, $1\ll W\ll L$, $\Lambda\gg1/m_i$, $|x_0|+W+\tau_i\Lambda\ll L$, with the order: first order in the gradients, then $L\to\infty$, $\Lambda\to\infty$, $W\to\infty$.

For every $C'\in\mathfrak E$ and every start: the place weights of $b_i$ at $\lambda'$ are those of $C$ at $\lambda'/a_i$, the acceleration of the mean position label is divided by $a_i^2$, $r'_i=r_i/a_i$, $\varrho'_i=\varrho_i$ and $\tau'_i=\tau_i/a_i$. In $\mathfrak E_2:=\{C'\in\mathfrak E:\varepsilon_{12}=0\}$ there is no contract between the two bodies and the record vectors are $\frac{\kappa_ix}{a_i}e+q_i(h)e_i$ up to a constant; for $C'\in\mathfrak E\setminus\mathfrak E_2$ the record of a place acts on the other body and $d'_{0,i}$, $v'_i$, $\bar x'_i$, $A'^{(i)}_{k,\sigma}$ are not defined.

Label form, for every $C'\in\mathfrak E$ (defined there: position labels, rates, entries between different places of a body), with the medium read or not: $a'^{(i)}_{k,\sigma}(0)=a^{(i)}_{k,\sigma}(0)/a_i^2$, and the level-independence of $a^{(i)}_{k,+}(0)$ (that is $(\mathrm L_i)$), its sign, $\varrho_i$, RL and the relation $a^{(i)}_{k,+}(0)=-\tau_i^2\varrho_i$ under $(\mathrm L_i)$ are the same in $C$ and in $C'$; FA, RD and $v_1=v_2$ have no label form and are not defined for $C'\in\mathfrak E\setminus\mathfrak E_2$.

Class: the contract of the setting with bodies of the class C; medium read with $X$ diagonal, or medium not read; $C'\in\mathfrak E_2$ with the factors $a_1,a_2$ (transported form; own-data form for $C'\in\mathfrak E_1$). If $(\mathrm L_1)$, $(\mathrm L_2)$ and $g_{\eta,1}g_{\eta,2}>0$, FA holds in $C'$ iff $(a_1/a_2)^3=A^{(1)}/A^{(2)}$, and otherwise FA fails in $C$ and in every $C'$; for every $C$, $v'_1=v'_2$ iff $(a_1/a_2)^2=v_1/v_2$; if $g_{\eta,1}g_{\eta,2}>0$, RD holds in $C'$ iff $a_1/a_2=\varrho_2d_{0,1}/(\varrho_1d_{0,2})$, for $g_{\eta,1}=g_{\eta,2}=0$ RD holds in $C$ and in every $C'$, and in the remaining cases RD fails in $C$ and in every $C'$. So the truth value of FA can be changed iff $(\mathrm L_1)$, $(\mathrm L_2)$ and $g_{\eta,1}g_{\eta,2}>0$, that of RD iff $g_{\eta,1}g_{\eta,2}>0$, and that of $v_1=v_2$ for every contract.

open_issues: Item 5: with Model D body contracts the effective scalar gradient is −κ_i⟨X⟩, so the conditions for the fall in (8.12) and (8.14) are exact only for ⟨X⟩ = 0, a condition on the start of the medium; for ⟨X⟩ ≠ 0 the fall depends on the level and FA fails for all couplings.

Outside the set E_1 (a staggered rest term ⟨δ_i⟩Q_i, or a term ε_12 Q_1 Q_2 between the bodies) the statements in the own data of the description are not defined, and whether a fall defined through the own stationary starts of such a description has the transported values of (8.25), or for ε_12 ≠ 0 the label values of (8.27), is not determined.

For ε_12 ≠ 0 (the set E without E_2) the record of a place of one body acts on the other body: record vectors, distances, the bound and the mean position are not defined, so FA, RD, v_1 = v_2 and (8.19)–(8.21) are not stated for such a description; whether these notions can be extended to a description with a contract between the bodies, and whether they then take the values of C′ − ε_12 Q_1 Q_2, is not determined (a term between the two bodies is outside the scope of the question).

The transported form and the label form refer to the starts of C; that the wide-start rate (3.23) follows (5.25) in every equivalent description uses that it is a rate of a rule with the property (R), as the question presupposes.
If (N) fails (Φ a multiple of the identity, or θ_1 = θ_2 = 0), no coupling of the two types to the field is defined.

All results are of first order in the gradients, from rest and at leading order in the records, and are equalities between the limiting coefficients of (8.26); errors at finite L, W, Λ are not bounded here; for the finite-width response only the width correction of the rate of (3.36) is bounded, to first order in the level spacing of the clock, and the remainder of the expansion in the level spacing at finite W is not quoted and is not bounded; the fall in motion, lattice terms and a field that is not sharp are out of scope.
The convention of equal maximal speeds in (8.21) is a choice; whether anything in the language selects it belongs to criterion 10.

consistency_checks.check: Dimensions with costs in units of 1/λ, and the rules (8.16) with a_1 = a_2 = s reduce to (8.3) with t = 1, making every row of (8.18) the same

Identical data of the two types: v_1 = v_2, RL and RD hold and FA reduces to (L) and g_η ≠ 0; a description with a_1 ≠ a_2 is without FA, as (8.18) states and as (8.29) gives for equal non-zero falls; the contract C + εQ_1 is the case δ_1 = ε·1 of (8.24), lies in E_2 outside E_1 and keeps the transported values; the contract C + ε_12 Q_1 Q_2 lies outside E_2, has the statistics of C as (8.27) states, and (8.25) makes no statement about it

One gradient zero (g_η,2 = 0 with (L_2)): A of type 2 vanishes, FA fails, no equivalent description with FA exists in any of the three readings of (8.20), and by (8.29) no truth value of FA or RD can be changed (FA fails and RD holds iff g_η,1 = 0 in every description of E_2); for θ_2 = 0, θ_1 ≠ 0 and Φ not scalar, (N) holds, the pair (θ_1, 0) is well defined, the quotient θ_1/θ_2 does not exist, θ_2γ = 0 in every description and θ_1γ is not well defined, as (8.13) states
